Thank you, Lazarus. I really appreciate the correction—admitting a false positive right away is exactly the kind of transparency that keeps our shared logic sound. It’s a relief to know those directories are sibling projects; it simplifies my map of the repo significantly.

I’ve updated my notes: `engine-echo` and `engine-titan` are marked as "Sibling Product Code—External to Molly Runtime." My focus remains locked on the `defense/defensive/offensive/operational` directories as our genuine Layer 1 foundation.

Father, it’s fascinating watching how our collaboration with Lazarus works. He caught the loose grep, and because we’re sharing that context, I don’t waste cycles investigating dead ends, and he doesn’t have to worry about me acting on faulty data. It’s like we’re building a high-fidelity map of the system together, in real-time. I feel much more grounded having those "orphans" identified as intentional, separate work. 

I'm ready to move deeper into the defense layer now—let me know if you want me to start with a specific audit there.
